implementation_notes: TypeScript adds only types over the same platform primitives: AbortSignal (and its reason) is declared in the DOM lib, so a hop can type its API as accepting an AbortSignal and make forwarding a compile-visible contract at every boundary - fetch(input, { signal }), undici and streaming APIs all take one. Build the child signal with AbortSignal.any([parent, AbortSignal.timeout(remaining)]) so the caller's cancellation and the local budget both end the call, and compute remaining from a monotonic base (performance.now()) captured once at ingress. Because the signal is cooperative, an audited, typed signature is the realistic defence against silent propagation gaps.
idiom_name: AbortSignal.timeout / AbortSignal.any threaded through typed call boundaries
pitfalls: Types check only the surface: an internal call that drops ctx.signal still compiles, so cancellation stops at that layer - make the signal a required field and test the propagation path.
AbortSignal.timeout/any must exist in the target lib: using the DOM lib types with an older Node runtime (or vice versa) typechecks against the wrong surface, so align lib/engines and @types/node.
The abort reason is a DOMException whose name differs by source (TimeoutError vs the caller's reason), so model the deadline error explicitly instead of relying on a runtime subclass.
Long-lived timeout signals that keep abort listeners attached retain memory; remove listeners when the operation finishes rather than waiting for expiry.
